notes.decision: Single-word line 1 of unclear function. Could be a running header element, an abbreviation, or a Lyc demonstrative ⲡⲏ ('that, yonder'). Translated tentatively 'That one(?)' with note. Same form recurs at line 3 opening, suggesting a discourse-marker function ('lo, that one') rather than a header.

Relative perfect 'who has X-ed.' ⲟⲛ taken as Lyc reflex of ⲱⲛϩ 'live' (= 'who has lived/is alive'), fitting context of an aging catechumen complaining to the apostle. Alternative reading 'who has returned' is possible but less well-attested.

Opaque idiom rendered 'What is the matter with you?' ⲁⲍⲣⲁϩ likely = Lyc reflex of ⲁϩⲣⲟ⸗ 'why?'; ϩⲃⲁⲗⲕ may include ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye' with possessive prefix or ⲃⲱⲗⲕ 'be angry/troubled.' The complaint formula introducing the catechumen's grievance.

Treated as proper name 'Pakhaios.' Could alternatively be a corruption of Greek ἀρχαῖος 'ancient' (yielding 'the Ancient Apostle' = Mani as senior apostle), or reflect a Sasanian personal name (Patikios, Pateg). Line 17 confirms the dialogue partner is the Illuminator (Mani), so ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓⲟⲥ functions as title or personal name for Mani.
ⲉϯⲛⲁⲛⲉⲩ parsed as relative + qualitative 'which is good.' The whole clause: 'the time which is good for a righteous one to be released' — i.e., when release from the body would be desirable.
Lyc verbal noun 'to be released' from ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ family, paralleled by ϩⲃⲗⲕⲉ 'release' in line 7. Soteriological release of the righteous from the body.

Future verb of harming/wronging. Possibly Lyc reflex of ϩⲱⲩϣ/ϩⲱϣⲉ 'press, oppress, wrong' or related harm-verb. Translated 'shall harm' to capture the catechumen's puzzlement at violence among supposed righteous men.
Variant spelling of ⲡⲫⲱⲥⲧⲏⲣ 'the Illuminator' (already in glossary). The intercalated ⲙ̄ may reflect a dialectal article-marker or scribal variant. Translation unchanged.

Negation pattern ⲟⲩ...ⲡⲉ with ⲉⲛ (= Sah ⲁⲛ) yields 'is not an established saying.' The Illuminator is judging the catechumen's complaint to be premature/unsettled — a question whose answer requires the parable that follows. Line 19 'You have repeated well' acknowledges the legitimacy of raising the question.

ϯⲥⲃⲱ 'the giving of teaching' (already in glossary as verbal idiom for 'teach'). With ⲙⲙⲛⲧⲥⲉⲃⲉ taken as 'from foolishness' (privative-source). The injunction: not to confuse genuine teaching with foolishness — i.e., not to misjudge the elect's outward conduct.
Conjunctive 2sg 'and discern.' From a verb of discernment/judgment, possibly Lyc form of ⲙ̄ⲙⲉ 'judge, distinguish.' The ⲕ- is conjunctive 2sg.m subject prefix.

'this tree which produces stench' — central image of the parable. The tree exemplifies how something with offensive smoke can yet have valuable fragrance, paralleling the elect whose outward conflicts mask their inward divine status (line 34).
Greek loanword κλάδος 'branch.' Standard botanical term, fits the wood-cutting image of the parable.

'the farmer of that tree' — invokes the agricultural-typological framework already established in earlier kephalaia (cf. ⲡⲁⲣⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ, ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲉ in glossary). The community 'nourishes' the tree-farmer because the tree produces valuable fragrance despite its smoke.

'of the elect; gods themselves are they' — the climactic correspondence: the apparent conflict among the elect is the 'smoke' of the tree, but their inner being IS divine (gods themselves). Direct correspondential identification standard in Manichaean teaching.

Read as Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲱⲛⲧ̄/ϫⲱⲛⲧ 'knead, mingle' (Sah. ϫⲱⲛⲧ; cf. Crum 776). The translation 'kneaded into the flesh of Sin' preserves the dough/baker imagery: the soul is mixed into the very substance of fleshly existence. Alternative readings ('joined,' 'tested') are weaker; the kneading metaphor fits the Manichaean motif of light-substance entangled in matter as kneaded dough.

Translated 'set yourself up against them' tentatively. Form analyzable as reflexive on ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise/set up' (in glossary; per terminology guide, vertical/exposing semantics preserved) — 'do not raise yourself against them' fits the list of forbidden hostile reactions. Alternative readings: 'remove yourself from them' (cf. ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲟ ⲁⲡⲁϩ in glossary); 'yield yourself to them' (cf. ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲁⲩ ⲁⲣⲁϩ in glossary). Confidence low.

ⲱⲱⲟ́ⲉ rendered tentatively as 'do violence to,' possibly Lyc reflex of ⲱϣϭ/ⲱϫϣ 'stretch out, harm' or ⲱϫϩ̄ 'defile.' Soteriological context demands a verb of harming the suspended Living Soul, since 'hands loosed at all times to X the Cross of Light' parallels the standard Manichaean ethics where eating/drinking/lust constitute violence to the Living Cross. Etymology uncertain.

Translated 'are filled (with grief) on your account.' ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill' + ⲛ̄ⲥⲁ- 'after, on account of' yields an idiom of being filled-with-feeling concerning someone. Context contrasts with the immediate negative-list (lines 28-29: they do NOT scoff, hate, distance) — so the holy ones' being-filled is a positive/sorrowful response, not hostile.

Reduplicated form of ⲛⲉϫ 'cast/throw' = 'cast at, throw at' = 'reproach, deride.' Standard Coptic intensive-iterative pattern. Translated 'deride' fitting the moral catalogue of forbidden attitudes toward the sinner (matched with 'hate' and 'distance themselves').

Idiomatic ⲱⲡ ϩⲣⲱⲕ 'keep silence' (Crum) with habitual prefix. The holy ones do not respond to the sinner with judgment but 'keep silence' — a pattern of patient endurance, which the next clause develops as speaking in love and Wisdom.

Lyc ⲱϩⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ in glossary, same idiom in different stem). Translated 'standing fast' to preserve the standing-firmly imagery foundational to Manichaean ascetic vocabulary.

ⲧⲥⲃⲱ rendered 'teaching' per terminology guide (CRITICAL: NOT 'insight'). The holy ones speak 'in the Wisdom of God' giving 'teaching' to the sinner — verbal idiom ϯⲥⲃⲱ 'give teaching.' The ⳨ symbol abbreviates ϯ throughout this page.

Translated as 'that they are sins' — picking up an ongoing speech from the previous page in which the forgiving brothers acknowledge the catechumen's wrongs as 'sins' that are now forgiven, set against the mercies they continue to show.

ⲥⲉⲃⲓ ⲛⲉⲙⲉⲕ literally 'they bear with you'; ⲍⲱⲥ ϣⲃⲏⲣ 'as a companion' — the brothers carry the catechumen as fellow-traveler. Preserves the Coptic 'bear (along) with' rather than smoothing to 'they treat you as.'

Translated 'the matter' — taking ⲡⲉⲁⲡ as a Lyc. variant on the ⲱⲡ/ⲍⲉⲡ family of nouns ('reckoning, judgment, matter'), introducing the topic-clause that follows ('that you may see no sins...'). Could alternatively be 'the judgment' or 'the reckoning'; chose 'matter' as most idiomatic in the conditional-purpose context.

Translated 'do not at all despise' — taking ⲛⲧⲁϩ as an emphatic intensifier (cf. Sah. ⲛ̄ⲧⲟϥ 'indeed') reinforcing the prohibition. Alternative parsing as causative-conjunctive 'let yourself' is possible but less natural.

Translated 'they being firm of heart' — ⲛⲁⲃⲥ tentatively read as a Lyc. qualitative meaning 'be firm/at peace,' fitting the contrast with ⲙⲛⲧⲧⲱⲛ 'contention' in lines 13-14. Lexeme not securely attested; awaiting parallels.

Translated 'the moment in which a contention shall arise' — ⲙⲛⲧⲧⲱⲛ 'contention' (in glossary) as the cosmic-affective event among the holy when the indwelling Old Man stirs them. The catechumen now grasps Mani's earlier teaching that conflict among saints is not their own action but the Old Man within them.
Translated 'they habitually receive injury' — ⲉⲡⲏⲣⲓⲁ from Greek ἐπήρεια 'insult, injury, abusive treatment.' The holy ones suffer mutual injury because of the dwelling of the Old Man in their flesh.

Translated 'they are stirred up' — taking ⲥⲉⲗⲉⲃⲗⲉⲃ as a Lyc. reduplicated verbal form denoting agitated mutual disturbance, in keeping with the iterative-affective pattern of pairs like ⲥⲱⲣϣⲣ̄ 'scatter' or ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defile.' Could also render 'quarrel' or 'agitate one another.' Etymology uncertain.

Translated 'fight together with us for the Land of Light' — taking ⲁ- as the directional 'for/towards' rather than adversative 'against,' since the Land of Light is the cosmic homeland the elect contend for, not against. The yokefellow image confirms a common combatant standing with the brothers.
